comparator.name: Art History
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 programme page and TER define one 180-EC curriculum combining visual art, architectural history and landscape history. The formal curriculum contains a common 120-EC first- and second-year programme, a genuine 30-EC minor, a 5-EC practice lab, a 10-EC excursion choice and a 15-EC thesis. The public page describes specialisation options, but the TER does not define mutually exclusive bachelor routes that change this reconstructed pathway.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad art-history, architectural-history, landscape-history, heritage, historical-movement, visual-analysis, conservation and transcultural core. Modern and contemporary art with museums and publics supports a distinct second curriculum. Landscape, ecology and cultural heritage supports a third curriculum with extensive environmental study. Architecture and Urbanism and Early Modern Art remain evidenced directions but are not attempted after the three-alternative maximum. Curricular-topic rows support these directions; illustrative and outcome rows remain search-only.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Western Art History directly surveys art-historical periods and visual analysis, with broader credits and scope.
Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean directly examines early-modern art and transcultural exchange, but not the full Groningen comparison course.
African Art & Heritage directly addresses heritage, colonial collecting and repatriation, while Groningen provides a broader preservation-theory course.
Heritage & Ancient Democracy directly connects classical art, architecture and heritage to public meaning, with a different thematic focus.
UCR has no dedicated historical course on European gardens and parks.
UCR has no dedicated course on Dutch art and architecture in global context.
UCR has field-based learning in several courses but no selected 10-EC art, architecture or landscape excursion equivalent.
Modern Art & Modern Museums directly examines modern and contemporary art and its institutional presentation, with different scope and credits.
Creative Communication Laboratory addresses contemporary creative practice and publics, but not the full studio-to-exhibition sequence.
UCR has no dedicated modern and contemporary architectural-history sequence.
UCR has no dedicated architectural-history course matching Architectural (R)evolutions.
Media & the Environment directly examines ecological meaning in visual and audiovisual culture, though it does not reproduce integrated art, architecture and landscape field study.
UCR offers environmental and visual-cultural study of landscapes but no dedicated course combining real and imagined landscape history.
UCR develops interpretation across art history, literature, media and philosophy, but no selected single course reproduces Groningen's concepts-and-objects course.
The genuine faculty-wide elective remains open choice space rather than being assigned an invented subject.
Writing Art's Histories directly develops art-historical research, visual analysis and academic writing, with different credits and course design.
History Research Seminar provides sustained independent historical source research and a substantial written argument, but is not a 15-EC bachelor thesis.
The genuine 30-EC minor, study-abroad or subsidiary space is preserved without inventing a selection.
UCR courses include applied projects, but no selected course reproduces the integrated art, architecture and landscape practice lab.

notes.text: Groningen provides a structured art-history sequence integrating visual art, architecture, urbanism and landscape history, including preservation, field excursions, practice and a compulsory thesis. UCR offers substantial related study in art history, heritage, archaeology, museums, visual media, history and environmental culture, but it does not reproduce the dedicated architecture and landscape-history sequence.
